title: Introduce sparse warmup manager and composite quant mapper for cost-safe prefill
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers with spiky, low-duty workloads suffer unit-cost inflation driven by repeated cold KV-cache misses and overly conservative quant profiles. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: (1) Sparse Warmup Manager (SWM) - a probabilistic, tenant-aware prefill/warmup controller that schedules small targeted warmup batches to seed KV caches for hot prefixes while keeping tail latency bounds; and (2) Composite Quant Mapper (CQM) - a runtime policy that selects quantization profiles per-shape and per-traffic-pattern using an empirical loss-budget model so we can safely prefer smaller quantization for low-impact tokens. Motivation: Reduce per-token spend on bursty tenants without compromising p99 latency or accuracy SLAs. Design goals: minimize additional GPU cycles for warmup, keep warmup failure modes isolatable, expose conservative safety gates, and allow rollback to current defaults. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-3112) [x] unit tests for SWM allocator [x] integration test for CQM policy [x] perf benchmarks run against representative tenant traces [x] migration script for tenant defaults [x] docs + release notes. Summary of changes (commits): [1] 5a8d1b3 - initial SWM controller and allocator loop; [2] 9c4f7df - composite quant mapper core + policy DSL; [3] b62a0e1 - telemetry and trace hooks for warmup attribution; [4] e3f2aa8 - safegates: loss-budget estimator and automatic rollback; [5] d90b4c7 - integration tests and deterministic replay fixtures; [6] f7a5c21 - tenant defaults migration CLI and docs. High-level files changed: ["services/serving/swm/controller.py", "services/serving/swm/allocator.py", "runtime/quant/composite_mapper.go", "runtime/quant/policy_dsl.md", "tools/tenant-migrate/migrate_prefill_defaults.py", "tests/integration/prefill_replay_test.py", "benchmarks/prefill/traffic_samples/tenant_bursty.json", "docs/engineering/prefill_and_quant.md", "helm/redwood/templates/swm-config.yaml", "observability/metrics/swm_metrics.prom", "e2e/workflow/prefill-smoke.yaml", "sdk/python/examples/prefill_example.py"]. Implementation notes: SWM is probabilistic and uses a leaky-bucket credit model per-tenant with configurable budget tiers. It prefers short prefix warmups (<= 16 tokens) and can be configured to avoid warmups for routes with strong latency SLOs. CQM consumes shape histograms and loss-budget signals from SWM telemetry to pick from available quant profiles (fp16, q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) with a bias toward more aggressive quant when estimated token impact is below a threshold. Safety: we add a loss-budget estimator that uses A/B shadow runs to validate composite quant decisions and automatic rollback if measured output divergence exceeds configured bounds. Migration: a tenant migration CLI safely annotates tenant configs with a recommended prefill budget and an initial composite quant seed; CLI supports dry-run and dry-apply. Benchmarks and results: synthetic replay of 10 representative bursty tenants shows mean per-token GPU cost reduction of 9.8% and 11.5% reduction at p95 cost, with p99 latency change within +0.8ms (within SLA). Failure modes: one observed edge case where extremely short-lived workloads cause warmup noise; we expose a "min-requests" gate to prevent warmup for tenants below threshold. Tests and CI: unit tests added for allocator and policy DSL, integration replay test included. CI runs: linux-unit-tests: pass, integration-e2e: pass, go-lint: pass, python-lint: pass, perf-bench: pass (benchmarks attached to PR artifacts).
